proofs.full_local_argument: Continuity on compact G gives points attaining a and b; nonconstancy gives b>a. Fix a minimizer xstar in G and put d=(f(y)-a)/(b-a), so 0<=d<=1. If d=0, the conclusion follows immediately because epsilon>0. Suppose d>0. For each real t with 0<t<d, convexity of G gives H_t={xstar+t(x-xstar):x in G} subset G. For any x in G, convexity of f and f(x)<=b give f(xstar+t(x-xstar))<=(1-t)a+t f(x)<=a+t(b-a)<a+d(b-a)=f(y). Hence H_t lies in the strict sublevel set, and therefore in Gprime. The affine map x maps to xstar+t(x-xstar) has determinant t^n, so Vol(H_t)=t^n Vol(G). Monotonicity of Lebesgue measure and the volume assumption imply t^n Vol(G)<=Vol(Gprime)<=epsilon^n Vol(G). Since Vol(G)>0, t^n<=epsilon^n, and since t and epsilon are nonnegative, t<=epsilon. Letting t increase to d yields d<=epsilon. Multiplication by b-a>0 proves the claim. This argument requires neither convexity nor closedness of Gprime, only measurability and the stated containment.

assumptions: G and f satisfy the stated conditions, so 0<Vol(G)<infinity and finite extrema a<b exist.
Gprime contains the entire strict sublevel set, equivalently f(x)>=f(y) for every x in G outside Gprime.
statement.objects_and_definitions: Let n be a positive integer, G subset R^n a compact convex set with nonempty interior, f:G->R continuous, convex and nonconstant, a=min_G f and b=max_G f. Let y belong to G and let Gprime be a Lebesgue-measurable subset of G containing {x in G:f(x)<f(y)}. Vol denotes n-dimensional Lebesgue measure.
statement.parameter_domains: n>=1 integer; 0<epsilon<1. This local statement extends beyond the source query-model window 0<epsilon<1/2; the extension is proved below.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every positive integer n, every such G and f, every y in G, every epsilon in (0,1), and every such measurable Gprime satisfying the volume premise, the conclusion holds deterministically.
